([[Blythewood, South Carolina]]) *Link Academy
([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = *[[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2022–present) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) }} '''Julian Phillips''' (born November 5, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. ==Early life and high school== Phillips was born in [[Killeen, Texas]] and moved to [[Columbia, South Carolina]] in the third grade after his parents, who were serving in the U.S. Army, were stationed at [[Fort Jackson (South Carolina)|Fort Jackson]].{{cite web|url=https://www.coladaily.com/communities/blythewood/blythewood-junior-julian-phillips-is-no-1-basketball-recruit-in-state-for-2022/article_1136792a-b4bf-11ea-be96-b76380b3a420.html|title=Blythewood junior Julian Phillips is No. 1 basketball recruit in state for 2022|website=ColaDaily.com|date=June 25, 2020|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He initially attended Blythewood High School in [[Blythewood, South Carolina]]. Phillips transferred to Link Prep in [[Branson, Missouri]] after his junior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/article253295328.html|title=Basketball recruit Julian Phillips to transfer to Link Year|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=January 17, 2023}} He played in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/lsu-basketball-signee-julian-phillips-named-to-mcdonalds-all-american-team/article_9b9f1008-7e27-11ec-9cef-a76362092b32.html|title=LSU basketball signee Julian Phillips named to McDonald's All-American team|work=The Advocate|date=January 25, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2023}} Phillips was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top 20 players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/05/auburn-basketball-misses-on-5-star-wing-julian-phillips.html|title=Auburn basketball misses on 5-star wing Julian Phillips|first=Nick|last=Alvarez|website=[[AL.com]]|date=May 12, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He originally committed to play college basketball at [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] at the beginning of his senior season and signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] (NLI) during the early signing period.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/lsu-basketball-recruiting-five-star-pf-julian-phillips-the-no-15-recruit-in-2022-class-commits-to-tigers/|title=LSU basketball recruiting: Five-star PF Julian Phillips, the No. 15 recruit in 2022 class, commits to Tigers|first=David|last=Cobb|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=January 17, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-branson-missouri-will-wade-basketball-5caa9b69ae164c61d5e761527964b7d6|title=LSU basketball signs highly rated recruit Julian Phillips|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 10, 2021|access-date=January 18, 2023}} After LSU head coach [[Will Wade]] was fired, Phillips requested and was granted a release from his NLI and reopened his recruitment.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33537750/julian-phillips-espn-no-11-college-basketball-prospect-released-commitment-attend-lsu|title=Julian Phillips, ESPN's No. 11 college basketball prospect, released from commitment to attend LSU|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 18, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2023}} He ultimately committed to play at Tennessee after considering offers from [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33905002/julian-phillips-final-uncommitted-five-star-recruit-2022-class-chooses-play-tennessee|title=Julian Phillips, final uncommitted five-star recruit in 2022 class, chooses to play at Tennessee|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=May 12, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2023}} Phillips also considered playing professionally in the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/news/julian-phillips-tennessee/iQ4ukscB9FHS/|title=Five-star SF Julian Phillips commits to Tennessee over Auburn, USC and G League Ignite|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 12, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} ==College career== Phillips entered his freshman season at Tennessee as the Volunteers' starting small forward.{{cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2022/12/08/julian-phillips-stats-tennessee-basketball-rick-barnes/69710758007/|title=Why Tennessee's Julian Phillips is nation's most effective freshman|work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]|date=December 8, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He was named to the 2022 [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] All-Tournament team after averaging a team-leading 13.3 points per game.{{cite web|url=https://tennessee.rivals.com/news/tennessee-beats-kansas-wins-battle-4-atlantis-finale|title=Tennessee beats Kansas, wins Battle 4 Atlantis finale|first=Noah|last=Taylor|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 25, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} Phillips played in 32 games with 25 starts as a freshman and averaged 8.3 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2023/03/24/julian-phillips-tennessee-basketball-nba-draft-future-florida-atlantic/70018609007/|title=What Julian Phillips said about NBA Draft, future after Tennessee basketball loss|work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=April 28, 2023}} After the season, Phillips declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.wbir.com/article/sports/college/vols/tennessees-josiah-jordan-james-julian-phillips-nba-draft-process/51-e2def424-88bd-41c6-a32d-c34b2b990086|title=Tennessee's Josiah-Jordan James and Julian Phillips will go through NBA Draft process|website=WBIR.com|date=April 20, 2023|access-date=April 26, 2023}} After taking part in the [[NBA Draft Combine]] and receiving positive feedback, he decided to remain in the draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2023/05/31/julian-phillips-nba-draft-tennessee-basketball/70275088007/|title=Tennessee basketball's Julian Phillips to remain in NBA Draft|work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=June 20, 2023}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links==
